Star Wars-level robots? I think we know how to make those now. What a time to be alive.

I read an article a few years back making the claim Amazon's purchase of Roomba allowed to to gather data by mapping the inside of residences through the vacuum's coordinates.  From that information, its GPS, and Prime account verifying the address, Amazon knew property dimensions, and could logically predict what furniture was in a room, along with dimensions and location of said furniture.  It would also track cleanliness through obstacles & amount of debris collected, and estimate number of people, and hours at home, etc.
 
From this info: 
- personas could be created, along with gAnalyics data using Prime account 
- products could be suggested without the resident knowing, based on room dimensions, life style, budget
- etc. 

As well, as long as the property existed, the next resident not owning a Roomba would still have its residence's dimensions on record. 

All this to say, if that is true,  Amazon may be in the best position for in-home robots given all the data it would have that could be used for training prior to the purchase of the robot.
